slot.subtopic: Work done by friction on incline
slot.brief: Work-energy theorem with a diagram: block sliding down a rough incline or released from a height with friction; use energy conservation between initial and final heights to find speed at the bottom or work done against friction.

stem: A $2$ kg block starts from rest and slides down a rough incline to a point $3$ m lower, reaching a speed of $6$ m s$^{-1}$, as shown in the figure. Find the work done by friction. Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.
solution:
By the work–energy theorem, $W_g+W_f=�\Delta K$.
$$W_f=\frac12(2)(6^2)-(2)(10)(3)=-24\text{ J}$$

draft.stem: A $2$ kg block starts from rest and slides down a rough incline to a point $3$ m lower, reaching a speed of $6$ m s$^{-1}$, as shown in the figure. Find the work done by friction. Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.

figure.description: Draw a straight incline descending from upper left to lower right. Mark the upper endpoint A and lower endpoint B, with a small block at A. Draw a horizontal ground line through B. From A, draw a vertical dashed line down to the level of B and label it 3 m. Draw an arrow along the incline pointing from A toward B.

draft.distractor_notes: A: treats the full loss of gravitational potential energy as work by friction. B: mistakes the final kinetic energy for friction's work. D: sign error in the work done by friction.
